items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen in walks of 10 to 19 minutes. You walked after 1 of your scored meals, but that's too few to see how it affects you yet.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: 81.8% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later. Across the program, sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners than after earlier ones in the same person, and 13.3 mg/dL more after a dinner at 8-9 pm than after one before 6 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a quarter of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: Eating dinner late, like you do 81.8% of the time, is linked to a bigger rise in sugar, especially when you eat between 8-9 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if that helps.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You're already fasting overnight for an average of 13.8 hours, which is a good habit to keep up. Fasting overnight has been linked to some positive changes in blood sugar in some studies, but more research is needed to understand its effects.
